title: testplan_sources
description: INPUT CONTRACT for env.manifest.json's env_topology.testplan_correspondence sub-layer -- the 'testlist / vPlan / coverage-model correspondence' fact source. It holds the three real lists a project already owns, exported to one shape: the TESTLIST (what the regression actually runs), the VPLAN ITEMS (what verification claims to be verifying, and which tests/coverage each item claims cover it), and the COVERAGE MODEL (which covergroups/coverpoints/assertions actually exist in the written SV source). env_manifest.py never invents any of the three; it COMPUTES the three-way correspondence between them and reports every broken link and every orphan. That computation is the whole point: each list on its own always looks healthy, and it is only the join that exposes a vPlan item claiming a test nobody runs, a covergroup nobody's vPlan item references, or a test in the nightly regression that maps to no verification intent at all. Each of the three arrays is independently optional, so a project can supply the two it has and get an honest PARTIAL correspondence naming the missing axis, rather than nothing.

kind.description: Where this file's content came from, e.g. 'regression_list_plus_vplan_export', 'vplan_xlsx_conversion'.

testlist.description: One entry per test the regression can actually run -- exported from the project's real testlist/regression list, not hand-listed from memory.

name.description: The UVM test name exactly as the runner invokes it (+UVM_TESTNAME). This exact string is what vplan_items[].tests must match -- the correspondence is a literal name join, never a fuzzy one, because a fuzzy match would manufacture links that do not exist.

tier.description: Regression cadence this test belongs to, e.g. SMOKE/NIGHTLY/WEEKLY (see dv_harness/regression_tiers.py). Null when untiered.

file.description: Path of the file declaring the test, so a broken link is traceable to a real location.

vplan_items.description: One entry per vPlan verification item -- exported from the project's real vPlan (see dv_harness/vplan_writer/writer.py for the workbook this is typically exported from).

id.description: The vPlan item's own stable identifier.

tests.description: Test names this item CLAIMS cover it. A claim, not a fact -- which is exactly why env_manifest.py checks each one against `testlist` and reports the ones that resolve to nothing.

coverage.description: Coverage-model item names this vPlan item CLAIMS measure it. Checked against `coverage_model` the same way.

status.description: The vPlan's own status text for this item, carried through verbatim and never reinterpreted.

coverage_model.description: One entry per coverage construct that actually EXISTS in the written SV source. This list must describe real declarations, not planned ones -- a planned covergroup listed here would make a vPlan item's coverage claim resolve against something nobody wrote.

file.description: Declaring file, ideally with the same file:line discipline the rest of this repo uses.
